image_description: A night-time photograph showing a woman holding a small hammerhead shark vertically by its cephalofoil (head). The shark's ventral side (white belly) is facing the camera. In the background, there are other people and a blue cooler on a boat deck. The lighting is harsh, likely from an on-camera flash.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the laterally expanded, dorsoventrally flattened cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The subject clearly displays the iconic T-shaped head structure characteristic of hammerhead sharks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows the ventral (under) side of the shark. Eyes are located on the dorsal (top) surface and are completely occluded from this viewing angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned near the lateral margins of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Small dark spots consistent with nostril placement are visible on the underside of the cephalofoil arms, near the edges.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior margin of the cephalofoil is straight to slightly curved with a central indentation in some species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The anterior margin is on the leading edge of the dorsal side, which is facing away from the camera and obscured by the holder's hands.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is streamlined and laterally compressed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body tapers smoothly from the head to the tail, consistent with a streamlined shark morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal coloration is grey to brownish with white ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible ventral side is distinctly white/pale, while the visible edges of the sides show grey/brown pigmentation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in dermal denticles with a rough texture.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Image resolution and harsh flash lighting prevent microscopic verification of dermal denticles; skin appears smooth due to specular highlights.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: First dorsal fin is tall and falcate (sickle-shaped), positioned anteriorly.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal fin is on the top of the shark, which is facing away from the camera. It is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pectoral fins are broad and triangular.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both pectoral fins are clearly visible extending from the body, appearing broad and roughly triangular.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a pronounced upper lobe.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail fin is visible at the bottom; the upper lobe is visibly larger/longer than the lower lobe, confirming asymmetry.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The skin texture appears unusually smooth and plastic-like in the center of the belly, lacking the subtle granularity expected of shark skin, though this may be exacerbated by flash overexposure.

artifact_observations.location: Junction of right pectoral fin and body
artifact_observations.reasoning: The connection point of the right pectoral fin (viewer's left) to the body appears slightly indistinct and 'mushy', lacking a sharp anatomical boundary.
The man in the background on the right has facial features that appear slightly warped and inconsistent with standard perspective, typical of AI background generation.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species classification and rule out generic shark misclassification.
To verify the structural integrity of the fin-body connections and check for melting artifacts at the boundaries.
To assess the realism of the lighting interaction between the flash, the wet skin, and the background subjects.
To ensure the hands holding the shark are anatomically correct and not fused with the shark's head.

focus_areas: Ventral skin texture realism vs. plastic smoothing
Anatomical correctness of pectoral fin attachment points
Lighting consistency (flash reflection on wet skin)
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'plastic' sheen on the shark's belly. Real shark skin, even when wet, usually retains some texture. If the classifier confirms 'hammerhead' but the texture auditor flags 'synthetic smoothness', prioritize the texture defect as an artifact. Also, scrutinize the fingers holding the head for any fusion with the cephalofoil.
